title: A Systematic Literature Review and CEC Quality Analysis of Single-Subject Studies on Physical Activity for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities
abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to systematically examine research trends and methodological characteristics of single-subject studies on physical activity interventions for individuals with developmental disabilities in Korea, and to assess their methodological quality using the CEC quality indicators. Method: Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 17 single-subject studies published in domestic academic journals over the past decade were selected and analyzed in terms of general characteristics, research methods, and intervention features, and their quality levels were evaluated based on the CEC quality indicators. Results: The results showed high levels of adherence in the areas of participant characteristics, intervention description, dependent variable measurement, and data analysis. In contrast, reporting was relatively insufficient in the areas of context and setting, interventionist training, intervention fidelity, generalization, and social validity. Conclusion: These findings suggest that while single-subject studies on physical activity for individuals with developmental disabilities in Korea demonstrate an adequate level of methodological quality in core components, more systematic reporting of research context, intervention fidelity, generalization, and social validity is required to enhance reliability and replicability as evidence-based practices.
